rv.q: Harper-Jackson is so good, he comes close to giving Frankie a credible emotional core, with a show-stopping rendition of That's Life as he laments the agonies of his affair with Ana Villafane's jaw-dropping Gardner. His smoochy I've Got You Under My Skin is reserved for serenading that goddess of the silver screen.
Sinatra the Musical is an inoffensive guide for newcomers.
But it's so far from exceptional. And for a big West End show with clear Broadway aspirations it should be so much better.
A lot of money has been spent here, but for what? To furnish a vehicle for the hits, which are duly trotted out, though often jarringly reframed for two mismatched voices.
That aside, what a thoroughly terrific evening of traditional musical theatre entertainment.

cn.t: This lavishly mounted Sinatra bio-musical delivers big band energy and hit songs, but critics find it lamely written with a misconceived narrative structure that fails to justify its existence.
